findings.title: The D7 flag embeds the agent's raw text without escaping, so an embedded quote can make the diagnostic read as truncated
findings.description: `tail_text` collapses whitespace, but `"` characters inside the response pass through unchanged, so the rendered `agent's final text: "…"` message can terminate visually mid-sentence (and the same string is the `each` batch report's flag reason via `_item_failure_reason`, and is logged at WARNING). The information is still present, but a reader cannot tell a genuine cut from a quote inside the agent's words. `src/squadron/pipeline/text_tail.py#tail_text` would be the natural single place to normalize the quoting, since it already owns the truncation marker and the empty-response rendering.

findings.title: `sq serve`-spawned SDK agents now also run with auto-memory disabled, a surface the slice's D10 policy table does not list
findings.description: The design (D10) enumerates reviews/judges, PR review, PR composer, pipeline sessions, one-shot dispatch, summary one-shot and audit, and lists `sq serve` agent spawning as out of scope. But `provider.create_agent` now always calls `sdk_settings_options(config.setting_sources or [], auto_memory=config.auto_memory, ...)`, and `AgentConfig.auto_memory` defaults to `False` (`src/squadron/core/models.py:73`), so a `sq serve` spawn that passes no `setting_sources` (which stays `None`, so the kwarg is still omitted) nevertheless gains `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`. This is consistent with D11's "every path that doesn't opt in gets memory off", and the behaviour is safe-by-default — but it is a user-visible change on a surface the policy table doesn't cover, so it deserves an explicit row (or a deliberate "yes, that too" note) rather than falling out of a default.

findings.title: The new test helper returns `object` for a session whose real type is imported two lines above
findings.description: `scripted_session` constructs a real `SDKExecutionSession` but is annotated `-> object`, which forces `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` on every use in `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py`. The project deliberately keeps `tests` out of `pyright`'s `include` (pyproject.toml, tracked as issue #50), so this is consistent with current convention and not a blocker; returning the already-imported `SDKExecutionSession` (and `ScriptedClient` as a `ClaudeSDKClient` duck type) would just remove noise from the new tests when that include is eventually widened.
